knowledge_point.title: Converting a Radical to a Unit Fraction Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
The radical $\sqrt[n]{x}$ can be written using a fractional exponent as ${x}^{1/n}.$

Comparing $\sqrt[n]{x}$ with $\sqrt[2]{3},$ we get $x=3,$ and $n=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\sqrt{3}=\sqrt[2]{3}={3}^{1/2}
$$

The radical $\sqrt[n]{x}$ can be written using a fractional exponent as ${x}^{1/n}.$

Comparing $\sqrt[n]{x}$ with $\sqrt[2]{1.5},$ we get $x=1.5,$ and $n=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\sqrt{1.5}=\sqrt[2]{1.5}={1.5}^{1/2}
$$

The radical $\sqrt[n]{x}$ can be written using a fractional exponent as ${x}^{1/n}.$

Comparing $\sqrt[n]{x}$ with $\sqrt[2]{7.5},$ we get $x=7.5,$ and $n=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\sqrt{7.5}=\sqrt[2]{7.5}={7.5}^{1/2}
$$
